title: introduce-stream-slab-acknowledger-and-ordered-event-silo
author: Priya Nair
description: Summary: Add a lightweight slab-level acknowledgement and ordered-event siloing mechanism to harden our HTTP EventStream (text/event-stream) ingestion path against chunked-transfer reordering, partial JSON emissions, and tool-call interleaving. Motivation: production incidents (see ENG-3142) showed rare but exploitable windows where a sequence of small chunks caused partial JSON to be delivered out-of-order to downstream JSON framers and the OpenAI-compat layer, producing malformed function-call payloads or dropped events. This PR introduces an in-protocol slab ACK ledger and an ordered event silo that: 1) assigns small incremental slab IDs to contiguous chunk groups, 2) buffers slab payloads until slab-level completeness heuristics are satisfied, and 3) emits an ordered, atomic JSON span to the existing SSE coalescer so function-call sentinels and structured output remain intact. Approach: implement a compact ACK/slot ledger in pkg/streaming/acknowledger, add a slab-aware reader wrapper to pkg/streaming/reader, and extend api/openai/compat/stream_framer.go to prefer slab-anchored boundaries when reassembling events. This is backwards-compatible: the ledger is only used intra-proxy; clients are unaffected. Changes include conservative in-memory limits and an opt-in config flag (REDWOOD_STREAM_SLAB_ACK_ENABLED) to allow staged rollout. Tests & validation: new unit tests for slab edge-cases, an integration scenario that replays recorded incident traces, and a canary deployment to a subset of streaming prod routes. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (linked) and Linear tickets created - [x] Unit tests covering partial JSON spans and tool-call interleaving - [x] Integration replay against incident trace - [x] Canary rollout plan and telemetry (latency/correctness) - [x] Post-merge rollback instructions and feature flagging Rollout: start with canary (5%) for client-facing streaming routes for 48h, validate JSON fidelity and tool-call success rates, then 25% for 24h before full rollout. Related: ENG-3142 (incident), ENG-3187 (streaming perf followup).
